title: Design and Technology Co-optimization Utilizing Flip-FET (FFET) Standard Cells
problem: CFET-based standard cells require excessive tap-cell overhead in FEOL to enable backside interconnect routing, hindering efficient use of BEOL backside wiring in sub-3nm nodes.
motivation: Sub-3nm scaling demands layout density and metal routing optimization; CFET's tap-cell overhead negates benefits of backside wiring for interconnect.
method: Flip-FET flips the lower transistor in a vertically-stacked transistor pair (CFET—complementary field-effect transistor), creating connection points (pins) directly accessible from both the top and bottom metal wiring layers without requiring tap-cells (helper cells needed for routing). To implement this, the optimization process synthesizes multiple Flip-FET cell variants with different pin layouts, optimizes their placement to minimize tap-cells, and rebalances wiring between the top and bottom layers.
key_novelty: Flip-FET eliminates tap-cell overhead by reversing transistor orientation to create connection points directly accessible from both wiring layers, enabling full use of the new backside routing layer.
contributions: Eliminates tap-cell allocation overhead in FFET designs
Enables efficient backside routing without wire congestion
Scales chip size beyond CFET with fewer routing failures
3-step DTCO methodology for optimized pin distribution and routing rebalancing
limitations: Comparison limited to CFET; impact on power and performance not quantified.
primary_theme: Flip-FET design and technology co-optimization for sub-3nm backside routing
